changes: Webhook exfiltration now requires the authority of the actual hostname-bearing DownloadFile URL. An unrelated webhook reference, a longer hostname or webhook.site used as user-info no longer supplies destination evidence.

MSBuild extraction accepts equivalent target casing and spacing in MachineName expressions. Truncated property groups invalidate prior bindings so an unvisited overwrite cannot leave stale hostname provenance.

Moved .NET stdio, console-option and process-start configuration references out of file profiles and hidden-execution claims to process fd/config and reflection subjects. Descriptions distinguish references and settings from enabled behavior or executed calls. All exact references were migrated; no parent-directory selector consumers were found for the moved profile leaves.
Added neutral managed Process.Start and Directory.Delete import/call observations. Standalone managed call observations are tested separately from import observations retained in package reports.

Changed the broad NuGet cleanup build-hook verdict to suspicious API clues. A hostile package verdict now requires the drawing-API claim, implicit cleanup context and absence of a managed runtime library asset. Honest declared cleanup and runtime-library variants do not receive that hostile verdict.
Moved the weak MSBuild hostname/download co-occurrence lead to a notable capability, preserving its matcher while removing the unsupported objective claim.
Replaced the internal-library description inference with a typed NuGet description-term observation. An internal security review is no longer described as a private library.
Added a notable postgres/postgres literal-credential observation for the supplied source template; it does not establish theft or a live secret. Clarified numeric PE timestamp field descriptions.
Corrected an invalid literal backslash escape in a concurrent Lua unit test so filefacts unit tests could compile; its intended test bytes were preserved.
